title: Maintaining Trap Seals to Block Sewer Gas
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water barrier, known as the trap seal, to prevent foul sewer gases from entering living spaces. A frequent issue occurs when self-siphoning or evaporation drains this water level below the dip. Professional tip: ensure every trap is properly vented within code-specified distance limits to break vacuum pressure during discharge. In rarely used fixtures, trap primers or periodic water replenishment help maintain this vital water barrier. Protecting the trap seal is essential for maintaining occupant health, safety, and proper system function.

Maintaining Trap Seals to Block Sewer Gas

A P-trap relies on a standing water barrier, known as the trap seal, to prevent foul sewer gases from entering living spaces. A frequent issue occurs when self-siphoning or evaporation drains this water level below the dip. Professional tip: ensure every trap is properly vented within code-specified distance limits to break vacuum pressure during discharge. In rarely used fixtures, trap primers or periodic water replenishment help maintain this vital water barrier. Protecting the trap seal is essential for maintaining occupant health, safety, and proper system function.
